claim: Lnc34a is a 693 base pair transcript composed of two exons, spanning nearly 15.3 kilobases.
source: Rapid amplification of cDNA ends (RACE) further identified a full-length, 693 bp transcript (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B). Northern blot confirmed the existence and size of the transcript in seven CRC cell lines and two colon cancer stem cell (CCSC) lines (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D). The CCSCs were isolated from two early-stage CRC specimen, and were functionally validated by serial sphere formation, tumor initiation, and marker staining (Bu et al., 2013). The original frozen stocks from the first passage were used in the study. The transcript is composed of two exons, spanning nearly 15.3 kilobases (kb), and does not contain a valid Kozak sequence.
evidence: The transcript length and structure were determined by RACE experiments and confirmed by Northern blot analysis shown in figures.

claim: Lnc34a has no protein coding potential according to the Coding Potential Calculator (CPC) and Coding Potential Assessment Tool (CPAT).
source: The full-length transcript has no protein coding potential according to the Coding Potential Calculator (CPC) and Coding Potential Assessment Tool (CPAT) (Kong et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: Computational analysis using established tools (CPC and CPAT) was performed, with citations to the methods.

claim: Lnc34a levels are significantly higher in colon cancer stem cells (CCSCs) compared to well-established CRC cell lines.
source: Consistent with the Northern blot measurement, Lnc34a levels were significantly higher in the CCSC sphere cells (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: RT-qPCR and Northern blot measurements shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C demonstrate higher Lnc34a levels in CCSCs.

claim: Lnc34a is enriched in the nuclear fraction of CCSC cells.
source: Cellular fractionation assays show enrichment of Lnc34a in the nuclear fraction (Figure 1D,E), and RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (RNA FISH) indicates that Lnc34a is mainly in the nucleus (Figure 1F).
evidence: Cellular fractionation assays and RNA FISH experiments demonstrate nuclear localization, as shown in Figures 1D, E, and F.

claim: ALDH1+ cells express high levels of CD133, another CCSC marker.
source: Flow analysis confirmed that ALDH1+ cells also express high levels of CD133, another CCSC marker (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A demonstrates co-expression of ALDH1 and CD133.

claim: ALDH1+ cells have much higher Lnc34a expression levels than ALDH1- cells in both CCSC1 and CCSC2 sphere cultures.
source: RT-qPCR showed that, in both sphere cultures (CCSC1 and CCSC2), ALDH1+ cells have much higher Lnc34a expression levels than the ALDH1- cells (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 2A and 2B demonstrate differential Lnc34a expression between ALDH1+ and ALDH1- cells.

claim: Lnc34a is asymmetrically distributed and enriched in the ALDH1+ (CCSC) daughter cells during cell division.
source: Co-staining revealed that Lnc34a was asymmetrically distributed and enriched in the ALDH1+ (CCSC) daughter cells, which were also CD133+ (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence co-staining experiments shown in Figure 2C, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C demonstrate asymmetric Lnc34a distribution.

claim: Lnc34a asymmetry in dividing cell pairs was confirmed in vivo in xenograft tumors derived from subcutaneously injected CCSCs.
source: Lnc34a asymmetry in dividing cell pairs was confirmed in vivo by RNA-FISH and tubulin staining of xenograft tumors derived from subcutaneously injected CCSCs (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: RNA-FISH and tubulin staining in xenograft tumors shown in Figure 2E and F demonstrate Lnc34a asymmetry in vivo.

claim: Lnc34a asymmetry in dividing cell pairs is more strongly associated with early-stage CRC, while late-stage CRC mostly has symmetric Lnc34a levels in dividing pairs.
source: Lnc34a asymmetry in dividing cell pairs is more strongly associated with early-stage CRC, while late-stage CRC mostly has symmetric Lnc34a levels in dividing pairs (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: Analysis of 23 early-stage and 22 late-stage human CRC specimens shown in Figure 2G and H demonstrates differential Lnc34a asymmetry patterns.

claim: Lnc34a knockdown decreased asymmetric division while increasing symmetric, ALDH1-/ALDH1- division.
source: Lnc34a knockdown decreased asymmetric division while increasing symmetric, ALDH1-/ALDH1- division (Figure 2I).
evidence: Pair-cell assays with Lnc34a knockdown shown in Figure 2I demonstrate changes in division symmetry patterns.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased asymmetric division but increased symmetric, ALDH1+/ALDH1+ division.
source: Ectopic Lnc34a expression also decreased asymmetric division, but increased symmetric, ALDH1+/ALDH1+ division instead (Figure 2J).
evidence: Pair-cell assays with ectopic Lnc34a expression shown in Figure 2J demonstrate changes in division symmetry patterns.

claim: The effect of ectopic Lnc34a on division symmetry was rescued by ectopic miR-34a expression.
source: The phenotype was rescued by ectopic miR-34a expression, suggesting that Lnc34a regulates symmetry through miR-34a (Figure 2J).
evidence: Rescue experiments with ectopic miR-34a shown in Figure 2J demonstrate that Lnc34a effects are mediated through miR-34a.

claim: The Lnc34a+ daughter cell has higher proliferative capacity and starts incorporating BrdU immediately when cultured in proliferative medium.
source: Pair-cell BrdU incorporation assay showed that, when cultured in proliferative medium (DMEM with 10% FBS), the Lnc34a+ daughter cell starts incorporating BrdU and enters into the next division immediately, whereas the Lnc34a- daughter cells does not incorporate BrdU (Figure 2K).
evidence: BrdU incorporation assays shown in Figure 2K demonstrate differential proliferative capacity between Lnc34a+ and Lnc34a- daughter cells.

claim: Lnc34a knockdown strongly suppressed sphere formation capability, which was completely lost after 3 generations of passage.
source: Lnc34a knockdown strongly suppressed sphere formation capability, which was completely lost after 3 generations of passage (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: Serial sphere propagation assays shown in Figure 3A and B demonstrate loss of sphere formation with Lnc34a knockdown.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression increased sphere numbers and sizes significantly.
source: In contrast, ectopic Lnc34a expression increased sphere numbers and sizes significantly.
evidence: Serial sphere propagation assays demonstrate increased sphere formation with ectopic Lnc34a.

claim: Ectopic miR-34a abrogated the effect of Lnc34a on sphere formation regulation.
source: Ectopic miR-34a abrogated the effect of Lnc34a on sphere formation regulation, suggesting that Lnc34a promotes CCSC self-renewal by targeting miR-34a (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: Sphere formation assays with ectopic miR-34a shown in Figure 3A and C demonstrate rescue of Lnc34a effects.

claim: Lnc34a knockdown reduced tumorigenicity in mouse xenograft models.
source: All five mice in the control group (injected with sphere cells containing the control vector) developed tumors. However, only three mice injected with sphere cells expressing shLnc34a1 and two mice injected with sphere cells expressing shLnc34a2 formed tumors, which are smaller than those of the control group (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: Xenograft tumor formation data shown in Figure 3D and E demonstrate reduced tumorigenicity with Lnc34a knockdown.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression enhanced tumorigenicity in mouse xenograft models.
source: All 5 mice injected with sphere cells ectopically expressing Lnc34a developed tumors, which are notably bigger than those in the control group.
evidence: Xenograft tumor formation data demonstrate increased tumor size with ectopic Lnc34a.

claim: Ectopic miR-34a expression abrogates the effect of ectopic Lnc34a on tumor growth.
source: Ectopic miR-34a expression abrogates the effect of ectopic Lnc34a on tumor growth, resulting in similar tumor sizes as the control group (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: Xenograft tumor data shown in Figure 3F and G demonstrate rescue of Lnc34a effects by miR-34a.

claim: Lnc34a knockdown decreased the ALDH1+ CCSC population in xenograft tumors.
source: Furthermore, we performed FACS on disassociated xenograft tumor cells. Lnc34a knockdown decreased the ALDH1+ CCSC population in the xenograft tumors (Figure 3H), while ectopic Lnc34a enriched the ALDH1+ CCSC population in the tumors (Figure 3I).
evidence: FACS analysis of xenograft tumor cells shown in Figure 3H demonstrates decreased ALDH1+ population with Lnc34a knockdown.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a enriched the ALDH1+ CCSC population in xenograft tumors.
source: Furthermore, we performed FACS on disassociated xenograft tumor cells. Lnc34a knockdown decreased the ALDH1+ CCSC population in the xenograft tumors (Figure 3H), while ectopic Lnc34a enriched the ALDH1+ CCSC population in the tumors (Figure 3I).
evidence: FACS analysis of xenograft tumor cells shown in Figure 3I demonstrates increased ALDH1+ population with ectopic Lnc34a.

claim: miR-34a is downregulated in ALDH1+ CCSCs and upregulated in ALDH1- non-CCSCs.
source: Opposite to Lnc34a, miR-34a is downregulated in ALDH1+ CCSCs and upregulated in ALDH1- non-CCSCs (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 4A and B demonstrate differential miR-34a expression between ALDH1+ and ALDH1- cells.

claim: Knockdown of Lnc34a significantly increased miR-34a expression levels.
source: Knockdown of Lnc34a significantly increased miR-34a expression levels, while ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased miR-34a levels (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 4C and D demonstrate inverse relationship between Lnc34a and miR-34a levels.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased miR-34a levels.
source: Knockdown of Lnc34a significantly increased miR-34a expression levels, while ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased miR-34a levels (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 4C and D demonstrate inverse relationship between Lnc34a and miR-34a levels.

claim: Lnc34a and miR-34a are mutually exclusive in the same daughter compartment and are present in opposite daughter compartments in more than 70% of CCSC1 and around 80% of CCSC2 dividing pairs.
source: RNA FISH showed that Lnc34a and miR-34a are mutually exclusive in the same daughter compartment and are present in opposite daughter compartments in more than 70% of CCSC1 and around 80% of CCSC2 dividing pairs (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: RNA FISH experiments shown in Figure 4E and F demonstrate asymmetric and mutually exclusive distribution of Lnc34a and miR-34a.

claim: p53 distribution is symmetric during CCSC division.
source: On the other hand, we only observed symmetric distribution of p53, the other miR-34a upstream regulator (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 demonstrates symmetric p53 distribution.

claim: 93.3% of tested CpG islands were methylated in ALDH1+ CCSCs, while methylation rate was as low as 2.2% in ALDH1- non-CCSCs.
source: Bisulfite sequencing was then performed to evaluate miR-34a promoter methylation in ALDH1+ CCSCs and ALDH1- non-CCSCs isolated from spheres. 93.3% of tested CpG islands were methylated in CCSCs; in contrast, methylation rate was as low as 2.2% in non-CCSCs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4G demonstrates differential methylation patterns between CCSCs and non-CCSCs.

claim: Knockdown of Lnc34a diminished overall miR-34a promoter methylation in sphere cells.
source: Knockdown of Lnc34a diminished overall miR-34a promoter methylation in sphere cells (Figure 4H), whereas ectopic Lnc34a expression significantly enhanced miR-34a promoter methylation, compared with the control vector (Figure 4I).
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4H demonstrates decreased methylation with Lnc34a knockdown.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression significantly enhanced miR-34a promoter methylation.
source: Knockdown of Lnc34a diminished overall miR-34a promoter methylation in sphere cells (Figure 4H), whereas ectopic Lnc34a expression significantly enhanced miR-34a promoter methylation, compared with the control vector (Figure 4I).
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4I demonstrates increased methylation with ectopic Lnc34a.

claim: Lnc34a knockdown increases acetylated histones H3 and H4 associated with the miR-34a promoter.
source: Besides methylation, ChIP-qPCR showed that Lnc34a knockdown increases acetylated histones H3 and H4 associated with the miR-34a promoter (Figure 4J), whereas ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased acetylated histones H3 and H4 (Figure 4K).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4J demonstrates increased histone acetylation with Lnc34a knockdown.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased acetylated histones H3 and H4 associated with the miR-34a promoter.
source: Besides methylation, ChIP-qPCR showed that Lnc34a knockdown increases acetylated histones H3 and H4 associated with the miR-34a promoter (Figure 4J), whereas ectopic Lnc34a expression decreased acetylated histones H3 and H4 (Figure 4K).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4K demonstrates decreased histone acetylation with ectopic Lnc34a.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression suppressed miR-34a expression in CRC cell lines Caco-2 and HT29.
source: Lnc34a also silences miR-34a in common CRC cell lines. Ectopic Lnc34a expression suppressed miR-34a expression, and promoted methylation and deacetylation of the miR-34a promoter in CRC cell lines Caco-2 and HT29 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 demonstrate miR-34a suppression in CRC cell lines.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a expression promoted methylation and deacetylation of the miR-34a promoter in CRC cell lines Caco-2 and HT29.
source: Lnc34a also silences miR-34a in common CRC cell lines. Ectopic Lnc34a expression suppressed miR-34a expression, and promoted methylation and deacetylation of the miR-34a promoter in CRC cell lines Caco-2 and HT29 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing and ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 demonstrate increased methylation and decreased acetylation.

claim: Lnc34a expression is lower in early-stage CRC and increases in late-stage CRC.
source: RT-qPCR performed in 23 early-stage (stage I/II) and 22 late-stage (stage III/IV) CRC specimens showed that Lnc34a expression is correlated with CRC progression. Overall, Lnc34a expression is lower in early-stage CRC and increases in late-stage CRC (Figure 4L, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis of 45 CRC specimens shown in Figure 4L demonstrates correlation between Lnc34a expression and CRC stage.

claim: miR-34a expression is higher in early-stage CRC and decreases in late-stage CRC.
source: miR-34a expression follows a reverse trend (Figure 4M, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4M demonstrates inverse correlation between miR-34a expression and CRC stage.

claim: The miR-34a promoter is more methylated in late-stage CRC than in early-stage CRC.
source: Consistent with Lnc34a methylation of the miR-34a promoter, bisulfite sequencing revealed that the miR-34a promoter is more methylated in late-stage CRC than in early-stage CRC (Figure 4N, Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Bisulfite sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4N demonstrates increased promoter methylation in late-stage CRC.

claim: Lnc34a interacts with DNA methyltransferase Dnmt3a, Histone Deacetylase 1 (HDAC1), and Prohibitin 2 (PHB2).
source: To understand the mechanisms via which Lnc34a regulates miR-34a expression, we performed an RNA pull-down assay with biotin-labeled Lnc34a, followed by mass spectrometry (MS), to search for potential Lnc34a-associated proteins. The DNA methyltransferase Dnmt3a, Histone Deacetylase 1 (HDAC1), and Prohibitin 2 (PHB2) were identified to be associated with Lnc34a (Figure 5A and Figure 5—source data 1). RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) using specific antibodies against Dnmt3a, HDAC1 and PHB2 further confirmed the interactions (Figure 5B).
evidence: RNA pull-down followed by mass spectrometry and RIP experiments shown in Figure 5A and B demonstrate protein interactions.

claim: Knockdown of PHB2 abolished the interaction between Lnc34a and Dnmt3a, but had no effect on the interaction between Lnc34a and HDAC1.
source: Knockdown of PHB2 abolished the interaction between Lnc34a and Dnmt3a, but had no effect on the interaction between Lnc34a and HDAC1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: RIP experiments with PHB2 knockdown shown in Figure 5C demonstrate that PHB2 mediates Lnc34a-Dnmt3a interaction.

claim: Knockdown of Dnmt3a did not affect the interaction of Lnc34a with either PHB2 or HDAC1.
source: Knockdown of Dnmt3a did not affect the interaction of Lnc34a with either PHB2 or HDAC1 (Figure 5D).
evidence: RIP experiments with Dnmt3a knockdown shown in Figure 5D demonstrate that Dnmt3a is not required for Lnc34a interactions with PHB2 or HDAC1.

claim: Knockdown of HDAC1 did not interrupt Lnc34a and Dnmt3a interaction, and only had limited effect on Lnc34a and PHB2 interaction.
source: Knockdown of HDAC1 did not interrupt Lnc34a and Dnmt3a interaction, and only had limited effect on Lnc34a and PHB2 interaction (Figure 5E).
evidence: RIP experiments with HDAC1 knockdown shown in Figure 5E demonstrate that HDAC1 is not required for Lnc34a interactions with Dnmt3a or PHB2.

claim: Lnc34a recruits Dnmt3a through PHB2.
source: These data suggest that Lnc34a interacts with PHB2 and HDAC1, and recruits Dnmt3a through PHB2.
evidence: The pattern of interactions observed in knockdown experiments (Figures 5C-E) supports this mechanism.

claim: The 1–267 bp fragment of Lnc34a is sufficient to bind HDAC1.
source: We then serially truncated Lnc34a and performed RNA pull-down assays to map HDAC1 and PHB2 binding to Lnc34a. The 1–267 bp fragment is sufficient to bind HDAC1, and the 560–693 bp fragment is sufficient to bind PHB2 (Figure 5F).
evidence: RNA pull-down assays with truncated Lnc34a fragments shown in Figure 5F demonstrate domain-specific binding.

claim: The 560–693 bp fragment of Lnc34a is sufficient to bind PHB2.
source: We then serially truncated Lnc34a and performed RNA pull-down assays to map HDAC1 and PHB2 binding to Lnc34a. The 1–267 bp fragment is sufficient to bind HDAC1, and the 560–693 bp fragment is sufficient to bind PHB2 (Figure 5F).
evidence: RNA pull-down assays with truncated Lnc34a fragments shown in Figure 5F demonstrate domain-specific binding.

claim: The 267–560 bp fragment of Lnc34a directly binds to the miR-34a promoter.
source: Although the 267–560 bp fragment does not interact with either HDAC1 or PHB2, the in vitro interaction assay shows that it directly binds to the miR-34a promoter (Figure 5I).
evidence: In vitro interaction assay shown in Figure 5I demonstrates direct binding of the 267–560 bp fragment to the miR-34a promoter.

claim: All three fragments of Lnc34a are needed for full suppression of miR-34a expression.
source: All three fragments are needed for full suppression of miR-34a expression (Figure 5H).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5H demonstrate that full-length Lnc34a is required for complete miR-34a suppression.

claim: Knockdown of PHB2 upregulated miR-34a expression.
source: We then knocked down PHB2, Dnmt3a and HDAC1 respectively, followed by RT-qPCR measurements of miR-34a expression. Knockdown of PHB2, Dnmt3a or HDAC1 upregulated miR-34a expression (Figure 5I–K).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5M demonstrate increased miR-34a expression with PHB2 knockdown.

claim: Knockdown of Dnmt3a upregulated miR-34a expression.
source: We then knocked down PHB2, Dnmt3a and HDAC1 respectively, followed by RT-qPCR measurements of miR-34a expression. Knockdown of PHB2, Dnmt3a or HDAC1 upregulated miR-34a expression (Figure 5I–K).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5K demonstrate increased miR-34a expression with Dnmt3a knockdown.

claim: Knockdown of HDAC1 upregulated miR-34a expression.
source: We then knocked down PHB2, Dnmt3a and HDAC1 respectively, followed by RT-qPCR measurements of miR-34a expression. Knockdown of PHB2, Dnmt3a or HDAC1 upregulated miR-34a expression (Figure 5I–K).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5L demonstrate increased miR-34a expression with HDAC1 knockdown.

claim: Inhibition of HDAC activity by SAHA increased miR-34a expression.
source: Inhibition of HDAC activity by SAHA and TSA also increased miR-34a expression (Figure 5L,M).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5N demonstrate increased miR-34a expression with SAHA treatment.

claim: Inhibition of HDAC activity by TSA increased miR-34a expression.
source: Inhibition of HDAC activity by SAHA and TSA also increased miR-34a expression (Figure 5L,M).
evidence: RT-qPCR measurements shown in Figure 5O demonstrate increased miR-34a expression with TSA treatment.

claim: Lnc34a binds to the miR-34a promoter via its middle fragment (267–560 bp), and recruits HDAC1 and Dnmt3a/PHB2 via its flanking sequences (1–267 bp and 560–690 bp) to methylate and deacetylate the promoter.
source: Therefore, Lnc34a binds to the miR-34a promoter via the 267–560 bp sequence, and recruits HDAC1 and Dnmt3a/PHB2 via the two flanking (1–267 bp and 560–690) sequences (Figure 5J).
evidence: The mapping experiments shown in Figures 5F, H, and I demonstrate the functional domains of Lnc34a.

claim: miR-34a is a well-known tumor suppressor in various types of cancers.
source: A downstream target of p53, the microRNA miR-34a is a well-known tumor suppressor in various types of cancers (Chang et al., 2007; He et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Chang et al., 2007; He et al., 2007).

claim: miR-34a has been shown to limit self-renewal of cancer stem cells.
source: Among its many functions, miR-34a has been shown to limit self-renewal of cancer stem cells (Bu et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bu et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2011).

claim: miR-34a mimics such as MRX34 are among the first microRNA mimics to reach clinical trial for cancer therapy.
source: miR-34a mimics such as MRX34 are among the first microRNA mimics to reach clinical trial for cancer therapy (Bader, 2012; Bouchie, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous reports (Bader, 2012; Bouchie, 2013).

claim: miR-34a expression tends to be silenced due to aberrant CpG methylation of its promoter in many types of cancer.
source: Loss of p53 function can lead to downregulation of miR-34a; however, miR-34a expression also tends to be silenced due to aberrant CpG methylation of its promoter in many types of cancer, including breast, prostate, lung, colon, kidney, bladder, pancreatic, and ovarian cancer (Corney et al., 2010; Kong et al., 2012; Lodygin et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Corney et al., 2010; Kong et al., 2012; Lodygin et al., 2008).

claim: Methylation of the miR-34a promoter is positively correlated with progression of colorectal cancer.
source: Methylation of the miR-34a promoter is positively correlated with and miR-34a expression is inversely correlated with progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) (Siemens et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Siemens et al., 2013).

claim: miR-34a expression is inversely correlated with progression of colorectal cancer.
source: Methylation of the miR-34a promoter is positively correlated with and miR-34a expression is inversely correlated with progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) (Siemens et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Siemens et al., 2013).

claim: Normal stem cells often divide asymmetrically to produce one daughter cell like itself for self-renewal and another daughter cell unlike itself to go down a path of differentiation.
source: Normal stem cells often divide asymmetrically to produce one daughter cell like itself for self-renewal and another daughter cell unlike itself to go down a path of differentiation (Neumuller and Knoblich, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Neumuller and Knoblich, 2009).

claim: Cancer cells, including colorectal, glioma, lung and breast cancer cells, could divide asymmetrically, generating progenies with different proliferation capabilities.
source: Recent studies have reported that cancer cells, including colorectal, glioma, lung and breast cancer cells, could also divide asymmetrically, generating progenies with different proliferation capabilities (Bu et al., 2013; Dey-Guha et al., 2011; Lathia et al., 2011; O'Brien et al., 2012; Pece et al., 2010; Pine et al., 2010; Sugiarto et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Disruption to asymmetric division in favor of symmetric self-renewal alters the balance between self-renewal and differentiation, which has been linked to neoplastic transformation and tumor growth.
source: Disruption to asymmetric division in favor of symmetric self-renewal alters the balance between self-renewal and differentiation, which has been linked to neoplastic transformation and tumor growth (Cicalese et al., 2009; Sugiarto et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cicalese et al., 2009; Sugiarto et al., 2011).

claim: Lnc34a directly targets the miR-34a promoter for epigenetic silencing by recruiting the DNA methyltransferase Dnmt3a via Prohibitin-2 (PHB2) and Histone Deacetylase 1 (HDAC1).
source: Here, we discovered that a novel lncRNA, Lnc34a, directly targets the miR-34a promoter for epigenetic silencing by recruiting the DNA methyltransferase Dnmt3a via Prohibitin-2 (PHB2) and Histone Deacetylase 1 (HDAC1).
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Asymmetric distribution of Lnc34a during colon cancer stem cell division leads to asymmetric daughter cell fate.
source: Asymmetric distribution of Lnc34a during colon cancer stem cell (CCSC) division leads to asymmetric daughter cell fate.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by experiments shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Lnc34a suppression leads to differentiation while its abundance leads to CCSC proliferation via symmetric self-renewal.
source: Its suppression leads to differentiation while its abundance leads to CCSC proliferation via symmetric self-renewal.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Lnc34a tends to be upregulated in late-stage CRC, associated with miR-34a silencing.
source: Lnc34a tends to be upregulated in late-stage CRC, associated with miR-34a silencing.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by experiments shown in Figure 4L-N.

claim: lncRNAs like HOTAIR and Xist have been shown to cause histone H3 lysine 27 methylation or lysine 4 demethylation.
source: Previously, lncRNAs like HOTAIR and Xist have been shown to cause histone H3 lysine 27 methylation or lysine 4 demethylation (Gupta et al., 2010; Tsai et al., 2010; Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Gupta et al., 2010; Tsai et al., 2010; Zhao et al., 2008).

claim: miR-34a targets factors of Notch and Wnt signaling pathways, both of which are essential for CCSC self-renewal.
source: This effect is mediated by miR-34a, which has been shown to target factors of Notch and Wnt signaling pathways, both of which are essential for CCSC self-renewal (Bu et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2015; Vermeulen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bu et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2015; Vermeulen et al., 2010).

claim: p53 knockout has been reported to reduce asymmetric division in mammary stem cells.
source: Although p53 knockout has been reported to reduce asymmetric division in mammary stem cells (Cicalese et al., 2009), p53 is not known to be a major regulator of differentiation and is symmetric during CCSC division.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Cicalese et al., 2009).

claim: Lnc34a provides an alternative, epigenetic mechanism that cancer cells can utilize to silence miR-34a without having to mutate p53.
source: p53 is a well-known upstream regulator of miR-34a, and loss of p53 function certainly downregulates miR-34a. However, the discovery of Lnc34a demonstrates an alternative, epigenetic mechanism that cancer cells can utilize to silence miR-34a without having to mutate p53.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the experimental findings showing Lnc34a-mediated epigenetic silencing of miR-34a.

claim: Lnc34a provides normal and cancer cells a way to decouple mir-34a mediated cell fate decisions from p53.
source: Lnc34a provides normal and cancer cells a way to decouple mir-34a mediated cell fate decisions from p53, which may be present in both undifferentiated and differentiated cells.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the observation that Lnc34a regulates miR-34a independently of p53.

claim: Ectopic Lnc34a can act both in cis and in trans.
source: The effect of ectopic Lnc34a suggests that Lnc34a might act both in cis and in trans, as have been observed for various lncRNAs such as Evf-2 and the capacity of ectopically supplied cis-acting lncRNAs to act in trans (Di Ruscio et al., 2013; Feng et al., 2006; Gomez et al., 2013; Jeon and Lee, 2011; Martianov et al., 2007; Rinn and Chang, 2012; Schmitz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the effects of ectopic Lnc34a expression and comparison to other lncRNAs, supported by citations.

claim: The CCSCs were isolated from two early-stage CRC specimens and were functionally validated by serial sphere formation, tumor initiation, and marker staining.
source: The CCSCs were isolated from two early-stage CRC specimen, and were functionally validated by serial sphere formation, tumor initiation, and marker staining (Bu et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the methods used to isolate and validate CCSCs, with citation to previous work.

claim: Lentiviral shRNAs have been reported to knock down certain nuclear lncRNAs efficiently.
source: To investigate whether Lnc34a regulates CCSC division symmetry, we first knocked down Lnc34a using lentiviral shRNAs, which have been reported to knock down certain nuclear lncRNAs efficiently (Castel and Martienssen, 2013; Di Ruscio et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2015; Xing et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating the efficacy of lentiviral shRNAs for nuclear lncRNA knockdown.

claim: The ability of lncRNA to target microRNA provides RNA circuitry more ways to increase the complexity of the regulatory network.
source: The ability of lncRNA to target microRNA provides RNA circuitry more ways to increases the complexity of the regulatory network.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the discovery that Lnc34a targets miR-34a.

claim: lncRNAs occupy the majority of the genome.
source: Given that lncRNAs occupy the majority of the genome (Mattick and Rinn, 2015), lncRNA/microRNA circuitry can potentially increase the complexity of regulatory networks.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Mattick and Rinn, 2015).

claim: Lnc34a contributes to CCSC self-renewal and tumorigenesis.
source: Taken together, Lnc34a contributes to CCSC self-renewal and tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the sphere formation and xenograft experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Lnc34a silences miR-34a expression in CCSCs by promoting methylation and histone deacetylation of the miR-34a promoter.
source: Taken together, the data suggests that Lnc34a silences miR-34a expression in CCSCs by promoting methylation and histone deacetylation of the miR-34a promoter.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the bisulfite sequencing and ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Lnc34a promotes CCSC self-renewal.
